tasks.description:
Define and document the core team structure for the project as specified in section 6.1 of the requirement specification. The team will consist of 4-5 people with clearly defined roles: 1 Product Manager, 1 Technical Lead, 2 Backend/CLI Developers, and 1 Quality Assurance engineer.

This foundational task ensures proper resource allocation and role clarity before development begins. The team structure is specifically designed to support the development of a CLI tool with Notion API integration.

The structure must be formally documented and communicated to all stakeholders, establishing clear reporting lines and collaboration channels between team members.
tasks.task_notes: This is a prerequisite for all other project activities. Team structure must be finalized before role-specific deliverables can be assigned. Consider budget constraints and availability of qualified candidates when assembling the team.

requirement_snippets:
Project Team (4-5 people)
├── Product Manager (1)
├── Technical Lead (1)
├── Backend/CLI Developer (2)
└── Quality Assurance (1)
constraints: Team must consist of exactly 4-5 people
Each role has a specific headcount allocation
success_criteria: Team structure with 4-5 people is formally defined and documented
All roles are assigned with clear headcount allocations

tasks.task_name: Define and assign Product Manager role
tasks.description:
Define the Product Manager role with complete responsibilities and MVP deliverables as specified in section 6.2.1 of the requirement specification. The Product Manager will be responsible for defining and prioritizing the feature roadmap, gathering user requirements and feedback, coordinating between stakeholders and the development team, managing project timeline and milestones, ensuring business requirements are met, and creating user documentation and marketing materials.

This role is critical for aligning technical development with business objectives and user needs. The Product Manager serves as the primary interface between stakeholders and the engineering team.

Key deliverables for the MVP phase include user stories with acceptance criteria, MVP scope definition, a comprehensive user testing plan, and a go-to-market strategy specifically for the CLI tool being developed.

responsibilities: Coordinate between stakeholders and development team

tasks.task_notes: The Product Manager must be onboarded early to begin defining user stories and MVP scope. Consider candidates with experience in developer tools and CLI applications. The go-to-market strategy should account for the technical nature of CLI tool users.

Product Manager (1)
Responsibilities:
- Define and prioritize feature roadmap
- Gather user requirements and feedback
- Coordinate between stakeholders and development team
- Manage project timeline and milestones
- Ensure business requirements are met
- User documentation and marketing materials

MVP Deliverables:
- User stories and acceptance criteria
- MVP scope definition
- User testing plan
- Go-to-market strategy for CLI tool
constraints: Exactly 1 Product Manager must be assigned
Must deliver all MVP deliverables before product launch
success_criteria: User stories and acceptance criteria are documented
MVP scope is clearly defined and approved
User testing plan is created and ready for execution
Go-to-market strategy for CLI tool is finalized

tasks.task_name: Define and assign Technical Lead role
tasks.description:
Define the Technical Lead role with complete responsibilities as specified in section 6.2.2 of the requirement specification. The Technical Lead will be responsible for architecture design and technical decisions, code review and quality standards enforcement, implementation of core modules, integration with the Notion API, performance and security oversight, and mentoring other developers on the team.

This role is the technical anchor of the project, responsible for ensuring architectural soundness, code quality, and technical execution. The Technical Lead must have deep expertise in the technology stack being used and experience with API integrations, particularly the Notion API.

The Technical Lead will work closely with the Product Manager to translate business requirements into technical specifications and will guide the Backend/CLI Developers in implementation.
tasks.task_notes: The Technical Lead should be the first engineering hire and should participate in architecture decisions from day one. Look for candidates with strong experience in CLI tool development, API integrations (preferably Notion API), and team leadership. This role is critical for establishing technical direction and code quality standards early in the project.

tasks.task_name: Create user stories and acceptance criteria
tasks.description:
Develop comprehensive user stories with clear acceptance criteria for the CLI tool MVP as specified in the Product Manager's MVP deliverables (section 6.2.1). This task involves gathering user requirements, understanding user workflows, and translating them into actionable user stories that the development team can implement.

Each user story should follow best practices (e.g., 'As a [user], I want [feature] so that [benefit]') and include specific, measurable acceptance criteria that define when the story is considered complete.

These user stories will serve as the foundation for sprint planning and development work. They must be prioritized and aligned with the MVP scope to ensure the team delivers the most valuable features first.
tasks.task_notes: This is a critical early deliverable that gates development work. User stories should be reviewed and validated with key stakeholders before implementation begins. Consider conducting user interviews or surveys to inform story creation. Stories should be sized appropriately for agile sprints (typically completable within 1-2 weeks).

requirement_snippets:
MVP Deliverables:
- User stories and acceptance criteria
- MVP scope definition
- User testing plan
- Go-to-market strategy for CLI tool
constraints: Must be completed as part of MVP phase
Must align with MVP scope definition
success_criteria: User stories are documented with clear acceptance criteria
Stories are prioritized and ready for development
Acceptance criteria are specific and measurable
dependencies: Define and assign Product Manager role

tasks.description:
Create a comprehensive MVP scope definition as specified in the Product Manager's MVP deliverables (section 6.2.1). This document must clearly delineate what features and functionality are included in the MVP release versus what will be deferred to future iterations.

The MVP scope should balance delivering core value to users while maintaining a realistic timeline. It should specify which CLI commands will be implemented, what Notion API capabilities will be exposed, and what limitations or constraints exist in the MVP version.

This scope definition will serve as the north star for the development team and help prevent scope creep. Any requested changes to the MVP scope after approval must go through a formal change control process.
tasks.task_notes: The MVP scope definition should be reviewed and approved by all key stakeholders before development begins. Be realistic about what can be achieved in the MVP timeframe. Consider technical dependencies and risks when defining scope. Document explicitly what is OUT of scope to manage expectations.

tasks.description:
Create a comprehensive user testing plan as specified in the Product Manager's MVP deliverables (section 6.2.1). This plan should outline how the CLI tool will be tested with real users before and after the MVP release.

The testing plan should specify: target user personas, testing methodologies (e.g., usability testing, beta testing, dogfooding), test scenarios and tasks, success metrics, feedback collection mechanisms, and a timeline for testing activities.

Since this is a CLI tool, the testing approach should account for different operating systems, terminal environments, and user skill levels. The plan should also address how feedback will be collected, prioritized, and incorporated into the product.
tasks.task_notes: Consider recruiting beta testers early from the target user community. Plan for multiple testing rounds: internal team testing, limited beta, and broader beta. Ensure testing infrastructure (analytics, feedback forms, bug tracking) is in place before testing begins. Coordinate with QA on test scenario coverage.

tasks.task_name: Create go-to-market strategy for CLI tool
tasks.description:
Develop a comprehensive go-to-market (GTM) strategy for the CLI tool as specified in the Product Manager's MVP deliverables (section 6.2.1). This strategy should define how the CLI tool will be launched, marketed, and distributed to target users.

The GTM strategy should include: target audience definition, value proposition and positioning, distribution channels (e.g., package managers, GitHub releases), launch timeline and milestones, marketing and communication plan, pricing strategy (if applicable), and success metrics for launch.

Given that this is a CLI tool with Notion API integration, the strategy should target developer and power-user audiences through appropriate channels such as developer communities, technical blogs, and relevant forums.
tasks.task_notes: The GTM strategy should be informed by competitive analysis and user research. Consider whether the CLI tool will be open source or commercial. Plan for documentation, tutorials, and example use cases to support adoption. Coordinate with user documentation efforts to ensure consistency in messaging.

tasks.description:
Design the overall system architecture for the CLI tool with Notion API integration as specified in the Technical Lead responsibilities (section 6.2.2). The Technical Lead is responsible for architecture design and technical decisions, which includes defining the high-level system structure, component interactions, data flows, and integration patterns.

The architecture must support the CLI tool's requirements while integrating effectively with the Notion API. This includes decisions about programming language, frameworks, dependency management, configuration management, error handling, and extensibility.

The architecture design should address performance, security, maintainability, and scalability considerations. It should be documented in a way that enables the Backend/CLI Developers to implement the system effectively.
tasks.task_notes: The architecture should be reviewed by the team and documented thoroughly before implementation begins. Consider industry best practices for CLI tools and API client libraries. Address authentication/authorization patterns for Notion API. Plan for testability and maintainability. The Technical Lead should provide guidance on design patterns and coding standards.

- Performance and security oversight

tasks.task_name: Establish code review and quality standards
tasks.description:
Establish code review processes and quality standards for the project as specified in the Technical Lead responsibilities (section 6.2.2). The Technical Lead is responsible for defining and enforcing code review procedures and quality standards that all team members must follow.

This includes defining: code style guidelines, code review checklists and procedures, testing requirements (unit tests, integration tests), documentation standards, version control practices (branching strategy, commit message conventions), and quality gates for merging code.

These standards ensure consistent, maintainable, and high-quality code throughout the project lifecycle. They should be documented, communicated to the team, and enforced through automated tooling where possible (linters, formatters, CI/CD checks).
tasks.task_notes: Standards should be established early, ideally before significant development work begins. Use industry-standard tools and practices where possible. Document standards in a CONTRIBUTING.md or similar file in the repository. Set up automated linting and formatting to reduce manual review burden. Consider using pre-commit hooks to enforce standards.

tasks.description:
Implement the core modules of the CLI tool as specified in the Technical Lead responsibilities (section 6.2.2). The Technical Lead is responsible for implementing core modules, which typically includes the most critical and complex components of the system.

Core modules likely include: CLI argument parsing and command routing, Notion API client wrapper, authentication and authorization handling, core business logic for primary use cases, error handling and logging infrastructure, and configuration management.

Implementation should follow the architecture design and adhere to the established code quality standards. The Technical Lead should implement these foundational components that other developers will build upon.
tasks.task_notes: Core modules should be implemented with extensibility in mind, as Backend/CLI Developers will build on top of them. Include comprehensive unit tests for core modules. Document APIs and interfaces clearly for other developers. Consider implementing core modules iteratively, starting with the most critical components.

tasks.description:
Implement integration with the Notion API as specified in the Technical Lead responsibilities (section 6.2.2). This is a critical technical component that enables the CLI tool to interact with Notion workspaces.

The integration should handle: authentication with Notion (API keys, OAuth), CRUD operations on Notion resources (pages, databases, blocks), error handling for API failures and rate limiting, pagination and data fetching strategies, and proper mapping between CLI commands and Notion API endpoints.

The integration must be robust, well-tested, and handle edge cases gracefully. It should abstract the Notion API complexity and provide a clean interface for higher-level application logic.
tasks.task_notes: Review Notion API documentation thoroughly before implementation. Consider using an existing Notion SDK if available and suitable. Implement comprehensive error handling for network failures, authentication issues, and API errors. Test with real Notion workspaces. Plan for API version changes and deprecations. Consider implementing request retry logic and caching where appropriate.

tasks.description:
Implement performance optimizations and security measures as specified in the Technical Lead responsibilities (section 6.2.2). The Technical Lead has oversight responsibility for performance and security, which includes implementing concrete measures to ensure the CLI tool is fast, efficient, and secure.

Performance measures may include: efficient data fetching and caching strategies, optimized API call patterns, asynchronous operations where appropriate, and performance monitoring/profiling.

Security measures must include: secure credential storage and handling, input validation and sanitization, protection against common vulnerabilities, secure communication with Notion API (HTTPS), and proper error messages that don't leak sensitive information.
tasks.task_notes: Conduct security review of authentication and credential handling. Consider using established security libraries rather than custom implementations. Implement performance benchmarks and tests. Review OWASP guidelines for CLI tool security. Plan for security audits and penetration testing. Monitor performance in real-world scenarios with network latency and API rate limits.

tasks.description:
Establish a mentoring program for Backend/CLI Developers as specified in the Technical Lead responsibilities (section 6.2.2). The Technical Lead is responsible for mentoring other developers, which includes knowledge transfer, code review feedback, technical guidance, and professional development support.

The mentoring program should include: regular 1-on-1 technical discussions, code review sessions with educational feedback, pair programming on complex features, architecture and design pattern education, and career development guidance.

This ensures that Backend/CLI Developers can work effectively, grow their skills, and maintain code quality standards. It also builds team capability and reduces dependency on the Technical Lead over time.
tasks.task_notes: Schedule regular mentoring sessions (weekly or bi-weekly). Balance mentoring time with hands-on development work. Create knowledge-sharing documentation and internal guides. Encourage questions and discussion in team meetings. Track developer progress and adjust mentoring approach as needed. Consider setting up a team wiki or knowledge base.

tasks.task_name: Create product roadmap and feature prioritization
tasks.description:
Define and prioritize the feature roadmap as specified in the Product Manager responsibilities (section 6.2.1). This involves creating a comprehensive roadmap that extends beyond the MVP to show the product vision and planned future iterations.

The roadmap should organize features into releases or phases, with clear prioritization based on user value, technical dependencies, and business goals. It should show what comes after MVP and how the CLI tool will evolve over time.

The prioritization should be data-driven where possible, informed by user feedback, competitive analysis, and technical constraints. The roadmap serves as a communication tool for stakeholders and a planning tool for the development team.
tasks.task_notes: The roadmap should be a living document that evolves based on user feedback and market changes. Present the roadmap in a visual format that's easy for stakeholders to understand. Include both features and technical debt/infrastructure work. Review and update quarterly or after major releases. Balance user-facing features with technical improvements.

tasks.description:
Manage the project timeline and define key milestones as specified in the Product Manager responsibilities (section 6.2.1). This involves creating a detailed project schedule that tracks progress toward the MVP release and beyond.

Key milestones should include: team formation completion, architecture design completion, MVP feature development phases, testing and QA phases, beta release, and final MVP release. Each milestone should have clear exit criteria and deliverables.

The Product Manager must monitor progress against the timeline, identify risks and blockers, and coordinate with the team to keep the project on track. This includes regular status updates to stakeholders and adjusting plans as needed.
tasks.task_notes: Build buffer time into the schedule for unexpected issues. Use project management tools to track progress (Jira, Asana, etc.). Hold regular check-ins with the team to assess progress and blockers. Be prepared to adjust timeline or scope if delays occur. Communicate timeline changes to stakeholders proactively.

tasks.description:
Create comprehensive user documentation and marketing materials as specified in the Product Manager responsibilities (section 6.2.1). The Product Manager is responsible for user documentation and marketing materials that help users understand and adopt the CLI tool.

User documentation should include: installation instructions, getting started guide, command reference documentation, usage examples and tutorials, troubleshooting guide, and FAQ. The documentation should be clear, accurate, and accessible to the target audience.

Marketing materials may include: product description and value proposition, feature highlights, use case examples, comparison with alternatives, and promotional content for the launch.
tasks.task_notes: Documentation should be written in clear, accessible language. Test documentation with real users to ensure it's understandable. Keep documentation up to date as features change. Consider using a documentation framework (e.g., MkDocs, Docusaurus). Include code examples and screenshots where helpful. Make documentation easily discoverable (website, README, built-in help commands).

Coordinate communication between stakeholders and the development team as specified in the Product Manager responsibilities (section 6.2.1). The Product Manager serves as the primary liaison, ensuring that stakeholder needs are understood by the team and that technical progress is communicated effectively to stakeholders.

This includes: regular stakeholder updates on project status, facilitation of requirements gathering sessions, management of stakeholder expectations, escalation of blockers and risks, and gathering stakeholder feedback on deliverables.

Effective coordination ensures alignment between business goals and technical execution, prevents miscommunication, and keeps stakeholders informed and engaged throughout the project lifecycle.
tasks.task_notes: Establish a regular cadence for stakeholder updates (weekly or bi-weekly). Use clear, non-technical language when communicating with non-technical stakeholders. Create a stakeholder communication plan that defines who needs what information and when. Document decisions and action items from stakeholder meetings. Shield the development team from unnecessary interruptions while ensuring critical feedback reaches them.

Gather user requirements and feedback as specified in the Product Manager responsibilities (section 6.2.1). This involves conducting user research to understand the needs, pain points, and workflows of potential CLI tool users.

Research activities may include: user interviews, surveys, analysis of existing tools and workflows, competitive analysis, and review of user communities and forums. The goal is to deeply understand what users need from a CLI tool for Notion API interaction.

The gathered requirements should be synthesized into actionable insights that inform the product roadmap, user stories, and feature prioritization. This is a continuous activity that extends beyond MVP to inform future iterations.

tasks.task_notes: Start user research early to inform MVP scope and user stories. Document findings thoroughly. Look for patterns across multiple users rather than optimizing for individual preferences. Consider different user segments (developers, power users, automation engineers). Plan for ongoing feedback collection after launch through usage analytics and user surveys.

This is an ongoing validation activity throughout the project lifecycle, with formal checkpoints at key milestones (architecture review, feature completion, MVP release).
